reviewers.summary: The parameter preservation and missing output directory tests now cover the prior findings. The production guard still relies on hostname naming conventions, so a production target with a neutral hostname can pass without isolation approval.

findingList.message: A01:2025 Broken Access Control: the production approval check can still be bypassed when the production service hostname has no “prod” or “production” label. Require an authoritative target classification before allowing the run.

evidence.codePathTraced: _production_target treats a target as production only when the environment says "production" or the hostname contains a label equal to "prod" or "production".
evidence.failureScenario: If the production ingest service uses a neutral hostname such as https://ingest.example/api/v1, a run with FLUXION_LOAD_TARGET_ENV unset and no isolation approval is accepted as non-production.

reviewers.summary: The round-two changes add assertions for preserved parameter values and the omitted output directory case, and add a production-URL isolation check. The prior findings are addressed; I found no new defect in the changes since the previous review.

The prior test findings are addressed. The production approval check still permits an unapproved production target when its hostname has no `prod` or `production` label and the environment metadata does not identify it as production.

findingList.message: A01:2025 Broken Access Control: production isolation relies on hostname-name heuristics, so a production target on a neutral hostname bypasses approval. Classify targets against an authoritative production target configuration.

evidence.codePathTraced: _production_target classifies the target using only the environment label and hostname text; build_load_run_config accepts any HTTPS hostname.
evidence.failureScenario: A caller supplies the production ingest URL on a hostname with no `prod` or `production` label and sets FLUXION_LOAD_TARGET_ENV to `test` or leaves it unset. The function returns a config without isolation approval, allowing the runner to target production.
